title: Mumbai Hosts Earthshot Prize Awards Tuesday, With Two Indian Finalists Chasing £1 Million
excerpt: Fifteen finalists from nearly 7,000 nominations contest five £1 million prizes at the Earthshot Prize's first India edition, hosted by Karan Johar; Prime Video streams the ceremony worldwide from November 30.
body:
• The Earthshot Prize Awards Night takes place in Mumbai on Tuesday, November 17, 2026 — the prize's first edition in India and its sixth overall.
  • Fifteen finalists, chosen from nearly 7,000 nominations across 169 countries, are competing across five categories; five winners receive £1 million each.
  • Two Indian finalists are in the running: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility (Clean Our Air) and Mahila Housing Trust (Fix Our Climate).
  • The ceremony takes place in Mumbai on November 17; Prime Video streams it worldwide from November 30, in more than 240 countries and territories and more than 40 languages.

Mumbai hosts The Earthshot Prize Awards Night on Tuesday, November 17, where five environmental innovators will each receive £1 million to scale their work. It is the first time the prize — founded by Prince William in 2020 as a decade-long initiative — has held its awards in India, after previous editions in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town and Rio de Janeiro.

Prince William and Catherine arrive in Mumbai on Monday for the ceremony, in what India Today, citing PTI, described as the couple's first joint overseas trip. William founded the prize to spotlight workable fixes for the planet's environmental problems, and the Mumbai ceremony is set to be the biggest edition so far, according to the organisers.

"These 15 Finalists give us genuine hope. I am looking forward to travelling to Mumbai with Catherine in November to celebrate their achievements."

— Prince William, founder, The Earthshot Prize

The finalists

The 15 finalists were selected from nearly 7,000 nominations from 169 countries, and are grouped under the prize's five "Earthshots." In Protect and Restore Nature: the Indigenous Desert Alliance, the Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative, and Bhutan. In Clean Our Air: Satellites on Fire, AirQo, and India's Mahindra Last Mile Mobility. In Revive Our Oceans: the Zero Emission Maritime Buyers Alliance (ZEMBA), the Niue Ocean Wide Trust, and the City of Barcelona. In Build a Waste-Free World: PFAS-Free France, Mother Earth Foundation, and the South Korea Zero Waste Movement Network. In Fix Our Climate: Ørsted, Pula, and India's Mahila Housing Trust.

Earthshot chief executive Hannah Jones called this year's cohort the prize's most globally representative yet, reflecting, she said, the leadership of the Global South and of communities closest to the challenges. The prize also notes that India is home to seven Earthshot finalists, including four winners — more than any other country.

Meet the Indian finalists

Mahindra Last Mile Mobility — Clean Our Air

Led by managing director and CEO Suman Mishra, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility is India's biggest three-wheeler manufacturer — and the only company, and only carmaker, among this year's 15 finalists. It has sold more than 400,000 electric last-mile vehicles, over 100,000 of them in a single year, and says those sales have avoided more than 180,000 tonnes of CO₂. Electric models now account for more than half of all new three-wheeler sales in India, the first vehicle category in the country to cross that line.

The pitch to drivers is economic as much as environmental: lower running costs can lift a driver's take-home income by 25–30%, backed by more than 900 sales and service outlets and access to over 10,000 public charging points. The company has also trained 500 women to drive and repair electric three-wheelers, and is aiming for one million electric vehicles on India's roads by 2031.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=L7w3VkCdOas

Mahila Housing Trust — Fix Our Climate

Mahila Housing Trust, led by director Bijal Brahmbhatt, works on the other end of the climate problem: not stopping the heat, but helping the women who live with the worst of it survive it. Its centrepiece is an affordable solar-reflective roof coating that can cut indoor temperatures by up to 5°C in the metal- and concrete-roofed homes of low-income settlements — 36,500 cool roofs so far, demonstrated house by house by women trained as Climate Saathis, and written into Heat Action Plans in cities including Jaipur, Indore and Jalgaon.

Cooling a home does not replace a lost day's wages, so since 2018 the trust has also pioneered parametric climate insurance: when independently measured temperatures cross an agreed threshold, payments arrive automatically, with no loss to prove. Some 49,000 women across Delhi and Gujarat are covered. By 2030 the trust aims to protect three million households and insure 300,000 women.

The night itself

Filmmaker Karan Johar hosts the ceremony. Mint reports a lineup including Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, Rami Malek, Sonam Kapoor and Simone Ashley, a performance by Shreya Ghoshal, and British band Take That performing in India for the first time, and Earthshot ambassadors Robert Irwin and Nomzamo Mbatha taking part, with around 5,000 guests expected. The Serum Institute of India is the principal sponsor of the 2026 Earthshot Prize Summit in Mumbai, and the city was selected during the inaugural Mumbai Climate Week. The full finalist list and the solutions behind each entry are on the Earthshot Prize website.

What happens next

The five winners are announced on the night and each receives £1 million to scale their solution. For diaspora readers, the full ceremony streams on Prime Video — the event's exclusive streaming partner — from November 30, in more than 240 countries and territories, so the Mumbai night is watchable from the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf two weeks after the winners are named.
